keepsakes.name: A spare ballpoint tip
keepsakes.text: From the workshop model in the Nexus. Three objects, three different kinds of 'first'.
keepsakes.where: The Nexus: label the pen display.
keepsakes.use: A pen tip can write. Somewhere there is a journal waiting for a new entry.

keepsakes.name: A spare lens ring
keepsakes.text: From the Date Lens. It reminds you to ask: a date of what?
keepsakes.where: The Nexus: get the Date Lens.
keepsakes.use: Your lens shows when ink was laid down. Try it on old writing.

keepsakes.name: A brass key-plate
keepsakes.text: From the Timeline Door. It says: dates of telling only.
keepsakes.where: The Nexus: open the Timeline Door.
keepsakes.use: Nexus locks are made by one maker. This plate may fit another Nexus lock.

keepsakes.name: A moth lamp
keepsakes.text: A little lamp. The Glimmermoth visits it sometimes, but only when you sit still and watch.
keepsakes.use: It glows in the dark. Somewhere, a dark corner hides something.

keepsakes.name: A 'So what?' stone
keepsakes.text: From the Alcove of Firsts. A display is not finished until it says why it matters.
keepsakes.where: The Nexus: finish the Alcove of Firsts.
keepsakes.use: Hold it when someone leaves you a message. Ask: so what?

keepsakes.name: The 32nd piece of glass
keepsakes.text: Glazier Imre cut it for a pane that never came. A pattern is a guess until a proof holds for every case.
keepsakes.use: One piece of glass is still missing from a small round window somewhere.

keepsakes.name: A copy of a notice
keepsakes.text: From the Sign-Smith's board. One comma changed what the whole market did.
keepsakes.use: Compare it with older notices. Did Emberford always write like this?

keepsakes.name: A knot of citation thread
keepsakes.text: From the Citation Thread bridge. Author, title, container, publisher, date, page.
keepsakes.use: Look for cards tied the same way, and ask whoever is cited.

keepsakes.name: A guild check weight
keepsakes.text: From the Weigh-House. 'The same measure for every hand.'
keepsakes.use: One true weight checks the others. Hesper may know who made it.

keepsakes.name: A twist of red and gold yarn
keepsakes.text: From the practice clue board. Red to challenge, gold to support.
keepsakes.use: Red and gold yarn helps you read another person's clue board.

keepsakes.name: A little copper pot
keepsakes.text: A gift from the cart driver. Each witness saw one part; together the parts made a fair account.
keepsakes.use: Someone in the market may recognise this pot. A cold stove may want it too.

keepsakes.name: Kip's map of good places
keepsakes.text: A warm step, an echo and a climbing tree. No official map shows them; this one does.
keepsakes.use: It shows Emberford today. Compare it with an older map, and show Kip.

keepsakes.name: A spare brass cog
keepsakes.text: From Mara's sorter. A machine that learns from examples knows only what its examples show.
keepsakes.use: A stopped clock somewhere may need it.

keepsakes.name: A measuring knot
keepsakes.text: From Idris's rope to the echo wall. Two methods that agree are strong evidence; a delay in every try needs its own check.
keepsakes.use: Use it on a line on a wall.

keepsakes.name: A tiny jar of soot
keepsakes.text: From the Founders' Plaque. Even dirt can be evidence of where a thing has been.
keepsakes.use: Soot shows dents in paper. Try it on a blank sheet that is not quite blank.

keepsakes.name: A splinter of an old sign
keepsakes.text: From Corvan's old sign board. Whatever it said, it said too much.
keepsakes.use: Corvan may want to talk about his old sign.

keepsakes.name: A quiet rumour shard
keepsakes.text: From the Shattering Rumour. A story is easier to check when you know where it began.
keepsakes.use: Show it to the tea seller. Rumours are also collected somewhere else.

keepsakes.name: A knotted rope end
keepsakes.text: From the East Well. The knots measure; the people decide.
keepsakes.where: Emberford: the East Well side quest.
keepsakes.use: Ask Efua who first cut the knots. Old buckets keep old ropes.

keepsakes.name: A blank survey slip
keepsakes.text: From the toll box. Who you ask, and how you ask, are part of the answer.
keepsakes.use: Show Orrin how the council could ask. Old slips may show an old mistake.

keepsakes.name: A stub of slate chalk
keepsakes.text: From the ferry slate. Loma, tavi, kethe, belun: four words that English needed a phrase for.
keepsakes.use: Say 'tavi' to Sefa. Chalk helps you trace notes written in the cant.

keepsakes.name: A small card frame
keepsakes.text: Nell cut it for you. Hold it up to anything, and ask what is outside it.
keepsakes.where: Emberford: Nell's easel in the market.
keepsakes.use: Hold it up to a painting and then lower it. What was outside the frame?

keepsakes.name: A tiny brass bell
keepsakes.text: Maren's thanks. It rings one note. It does not climb, however long you listen.
keepsakes.where: Emberford: Maren's bell rope by the gatehouse.
keepsakes.use: It rings one note. Another bell may answer it.

keepsakes.name: A pocket weather glass
keepsakes.text: From Fisher Noa. 'It does not tell you what will happen. It tells you how sure to be.'
keepsakes.where: Emberford: Noa's forecast board by the east well.
keepsakes.use: Compare it with another weather glass. Instruments drift.

keepsakes.name: A wax copy of the seal
keepsakes.text: The Guardians' seal, found at the end of the chapter.
keepsakes.use: Compare it with another Guardian's mark, and ask Ise.
